- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes, then sharply drop — suggesting overshoot and failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the latter half of the 30d window, particularly after mid-term peaks.
- Forecast bias is stronger in periods with high volatility or sharp downward moves — model fails to adjust downward quickly enough.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops — often takes 2–3 days to correct downward trend.
- In cases of sustained upward trends, model overreacts to short-term volatility and fails to smooth out the mean reversion.
- Forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 5–7 days, then gradually adjust — suggesting a “warm-up” bias or delayed calibration.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections after spikes — often misses the depth of the drop.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to overestimate future price stability — fails to account for hidden volatility or policy shocks.
- Model does not adequately adjust for seasonal or policy-driven price shifts — e.g., ETS auction timing or regulatory changes.
